title: French household confidence remains depressed while precautionary saving stays elevated and major-purchase room remains weak
source_unit: INSEE, Monthly consumer confidence survey, September 2026
geography: France; approximately 2,000 households surveyed by telephone during August 26–September 17, 2026

denominator.unit: approximately French households surveyed by telephone

household_confidence.unit: INSEE synthetic household-confidence index; long-term average 100

savings_climate.unit: INSEE synthetic savings-climate index; long-term average 100

monthly_change.value: confidence was stable at 86 while the savings-climate index fell four points from August's 125

precautionary_room.value: high saving climate coexists with deteriorated confidence, indicating caution does not equal comfortable household room

observations.method: Monthly consumer confidence survey using seasonally adjusted balances and factor-analysis synthetic indexes; around 2,000 households interviewed by telephone in the first three weeks of the month.
observations.uncertainty: Synthetic indexes summarize correlated opinions and are not direct measures of saving balances, consumption, income, or household-level financial behavior.
observations.subgroup: French households participating in the monthly confidence survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high savings-climate index may reflect opportunity or intention to save rather than actual saving, and low confidence may coexist with adequate resources for some households.

denominator.unit: approximately French households surveyed by telephone

major_purchase_intentions.unit: seasonally adjusted balance of opinion on whether it is a good time for major purchases; long-term average -16

past_financial_situation.unit: balance of opinion on past personal financial situation; long-term average -21

future_financial_situation.unit: balance of opinion on expected personal financial situation; long-term average -7

consumption_route.value: weak major-purchase willingness persists even as savings capacity indicators remain above long-term averages

observations.method: Seasonally adjusted monthly opinion balances within the INSEE household confidence survey.
observations.uncertainty: Balances are differences between positive and negative responses and are not percentages of households or realized purchase volumes.
observations.subgroup: French households reporting views on purchases and personal financial conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Weak purchase intentions can reflect interest rates, durable-goods timing, housing decisions, inflation uncertainty or preference shifts rather than current income shortfall alone.

observations.period: September 2026; saving capacity and saving intentions

denominator.unit: approximately French households surveyed by telephone

current_saving_capacity.unit: balance of opinion on current saving capacity; long-term average 10

expected_saving_capacity.unit: balance of opinion on future saving capacity; long-term average -6

savings_intentions.unit: balance of opinion on opportunity to save; long-term average 19

precautionary_behavior.value: saving intentions remain well above their long-term average even as current and expected household judgments are negative in other domains

observations.method: Seasonally adjusted balances of opinion from the monthly consumer confidence survey; synthetic savings climate combines current capacity, expected capacity and opportunity to save.
observations.uncertainty: The balance measures sentiment and perceived opportunity, not actual saving rates, liquid assets, debt repayment or distribution across households.
observations.subgroup: French households responding to current and expected saving-capacity questions.
observations.counterinterpretation: High saving intentions can represent unmet precautionary demand, wealthier household behavior, or a reaction to uncertainty rather than broad financial resilience.

observations.period: September 2026; perceived prices, unemployment and future living standards

denominator.unit: approximately French households surveyed by telephone

past_consumer_prices.unit: balance of opinion on price increases over the prior twelve months; up seven points in September

future_inflation.unit: balance of opinion on future inflation; long-term average -32

unemployment_prospects.unit: balance of opinion on unemployment prospects; down three points from August

future_standard_of_living.unit: balance of opinion on future standard of living; long-term average -29

cost_security_route.value: price salience and weak future living-standard judgments can sustain precautionary behavior even when some unemployment fears ease

observations.method: Seasonally adjusted monthly opinion balances from the INSEE consumer-confidence survey.
observations.uncertainty: The indicators are aggregate balances and cannot identify which households experience price pressure, unemployment exposure, or deteriorating living standards.
observations.subgroup: French households reporting views on prices, unemployment and future living standards.
observations.counterinterpretation: Perceived price changes and living-standard expectations may move differently from official inflation, employment or household consumption outcomes.

related_sources.claim: Official INSEE release, time series, methodology and September 2026 balances.
INSEE monthly household confidence survey series context.

boundary: This record adds a consumer-room route from price salience and confidence through precautionary saving, major-purchase restraint, future living-standard judgments and household expectations. It is a monthly repeated cross-sectional opinion survey with synthetic indexes, not realized spending, saving, debt, income distribution or causal household behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official INSEE September 24, 2026 release reviewed for sample mode and timing, confidence and savings indexes, major-purchase and personal-finance balances, saving capacity and intentions, price, unemployment and future living-standard balances, and index methodology.
